comparison.J_easy_label: post-hoc common score J_E = L_E + beta*S_E; the easy formulation minimises L only
comparison.hard_objective_label: min alpha*L + beta*S (the hard formulation's own objective)
comparison.integrator_note: the hard OPTIMISER integrates J with the trapezoid rule on 400 spline samples (the same active grid as the collocation constraints); the reported L, S and J of both routes are recalculated afterwards by the same polyline evaluator (segment sums, midpoint field values)

dijkstra_crosscheck.scope: shortest graph path between selected snapped cells only; exact endpoint connectors are appended and validated, not optimized over alternative connector choices

domain_easy.definition: n_on_masked_cell counts samples in land / NoData / outside-footprint cells (never allowed); n_on_infeasible_cell counts samples in cells whose node-level depth or slope breaks a limit (a discretisation-flag test, explained where it is reported)

domain_hard.definition: n_on_masked_cell counts samples in land / NoData / outside-footprint cells (never allowed); n_on_infeasible_cell counts samples in cells whose node-level depth or slope breaks a limit (a discretisation-flag test, explained where it is reported)

easy_route_discretisation.note: the easy route is measured on the discrete node-to-node polyline; a light 250 m moving-average smoothing of the same corridor is shorter, so part of any negative 'price of realism' is grid discretisation rather than spline smoothness.

easy_geometry.note: The easy problem does not constrain route curvature. The 8-neighbour grid route is a zig-zag polyline, so pointwise finite-difference curvature of the polyline is not meaningful; heading changes and the curvature of a smoothed spline fit are reported for information.

multistart.note: Distinct initial curves and solver executions differ; all executions are independently classified. Feasibility is not optimality.
multistart.feasibility_basis: independent nominal, dense depth/slope, exact spline curvature and domain checks for each execution

solver_strategies.feasibility_vs_optimality: Independent validation checks feasibility only, not optimality or a KKT certificate.

linear_solution.feasibility_note: collocation uses linear fields; dense validation below uses the baseline cubic fields, and no full independent linear-field classification was performed

interpolation.decision: the cubic tensor-product spline is kept: it is the smooth field the B-spline corridor is meant to follow, its interior depth overshoot stays below 10 m (1.2 % of the 800 m depth span) and the adopted route is linear candidate must also be checked against the baseline field. Linear interpolation is reported as the overshoot-free reference, not adopted, because it has piecewise-constant gradients that make the slope constraint meaningless on a 450 m grid

continuous_domain_easy.adopted_definition: continuously feasible = not inside a land/NoData cell AND interpolated depth and slope satisfy the nominal limits at the sample point

continuous_domain_hard.adopted_definition: continuously feasible = not inside a land/NoData cell AND interpolated depth and slope satisfy the nominal limits at the sample point
continuous_domain_hard.cell_flag_only_explanation: these samples satisfy the depth and slope limits at the sample point but fall in a cell whose node-level slope violates s_max; with a 450 m cell the node value is a cell average, so a route can clip the edge of a flagged cell while staying inside the continuous limits

curvature.note: sample-independent recomputation on a rebuilt BSpline; the parameter speed is not uniform, so the maximum is located by sampling t uniformly, not by arc length

runtimes.measurement_basis: median of 3 repeated calls of each operation on the same machine; baseline Dijkstra timer covers graph search, while repeated easy timer covers solve_easy including route assembly; hard repetitions are penalty continuations from the adopted point

beta0.note: beta = 0 removes risk from the objective but keeps the curvature and terrain constraints, so beta0 vs beta1 isolates the cost of risk avoidance in metres of added length.

edge_rules.note: `midpoint_corner` is the specification's rule and the baseline: a diagonal step needs (a) both endpoints feasible, (b) its geometric midpoint -- the point halfway along the segment, i.e. the average of the four surrounding node values -- inside the depth and slope limits, and (c) both orthogonal neighbouring cells feasible. `node`, `midpoint` and `corner` drop parts (b) / (c) and are kept only as variants.

margin_cost.note: a 2 % margin means the solver targets 0.98 x the slope and curvature limits, so that the independently validated route stays inside the nominal limits between collocation samples

verification.depth_convention: d is the GEBCO SEA-FLOOR depth (deepest = largest d). d_min/d_max limit the sea-floor depth along the route; they are NOT the tunnel depth below the seabed.

geometry.description: Exact endpoints and ordered graph nodes; adopted spline sampled on optimizer active integration/collocation grid. Interior B-spline control points do not generally lie on the curve.

sampling_protocol.note: HardProblem sets its active spline grid to n_constraint_samples; both objective integration and collocation use it.

easy.definition: feasible = collocation constraints at nominal limits AND dense depth AND dense slope AND exact spline curvature AND inside the valid data domain AND finite, strictly positive interpolated depth

hard.definition: feasible = collocation constraints at nominal limits AND dense depth AND dense slope AND exact spline curvature AND inside the valid data domain AND finite, strictly positive interpolated depth

kappa_exact_hard.note: sample-independent recomputation on a rebuilt BSpline; the parameter speed is not uniform, so the maximum is located by sampling t uniformly, not by arc length

depth_leakage.policy: an interpolated depth <= 0 means the interpolant implied land; it is treated as infeasible (the constraint d >= d_min with d_min > 0 rejects it), never clipped to a small positive value
depth_leakage.note: depth is interpolated from ocean samples only; the two columns show the cubic and the linear depth interpolants on identical probes.

data_meta.resampling_policy: strict bilinear: a target point is valid only if every weighted source corner is a valid ocean cell; no extrapolation, no blending of land/NoData
data_meta.nodata_policy: z <= -100000.0 or non-finite -> missing; land (z >= 0) masked; both applied to the SOURCE raster before resampling
data_meta.edge_policy: inside the footprint but outside the outermost source cell centre, the edge cell is replicated (no extrapolation)
